title: A Two Level Neural Approach Combining Off-Chip Prediction with Adaptive Prefetch Filtering
problem: Contemporary applications with large data footprints frequently incur off-chip DRAM accesses that degrade performance and energy efficiency. The challenge is accurately predicting cache misses to DRAM and selectively filtering prefetches at the L1D cache to reduce bandwidth waste.
motivation: Reducing DRAM traffic through intelligent prediction and prefetch filtering is critical for improving performance and energy efficiency in memory-bound applications.
method: The system chains two neural network predictors (perceptrons) together. The first uses software memory addresses plus timing information to predict when data will come from main memory (off-chip). The second uses those predictions and hardware memory addresses to control which prefetches reach the L1 cache. This fits in just 7 kilobytes of silicon.
key_novelty: First hardware design to combine off-chip prediction with L1 cache prefetch filtering through a two-stage neural network, where the first stage's predictions directly inform the second stage's filtering decisions.
contributions: Two-level perceptron architecture unifying off-chip prediction with adaptive prefetch filtering at L1D
Novel selective delay component for accurate off-chip access prediction using virtual addresses
Leveraging off-chip predictions to guide prefetch filtering decisions
Compact hardware requiring only 7KB storage achieving 6.2% and 11.8% speedups on single and multi-core workloads
primary_theme: Neural memory access prediction and adaptive prefetch filtering
